ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a home, not a camp
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Turn the camp into a home, one step at a time: first a real bed for everyone instead of a sleeping spot or the floor, then a proper room to eat in, with a table.

plain.li: We've been sleeping on the ground long enough. Beds first, then a room to eat in. Then it's a home.
Right now this is a camp with walls. I'd like it to be a place we live.
[rain] Another night on a wet floor. Proper beds, please, and a roof over the table.
[small] There aren't many of us. That makes it easier to give every one of us a bed.
[tribal] A people with a home tell stories by its fire. We're still telling ours on the bare ground.

warm.li: Everyone should wake up in a real bed and sit down to a real table. It isn't much to ask.

blunt.li: My back hurts from the floor. Beds. Then a table. That's my plan.

cheerful.li: I've already picked where my bed goes, and I'm going to sleep in it for a week.

gloomy.li: We might not last. If we do, I'd rather not have spent it sleeping in the dirt.

cold.li: Rest and meals improve everything else we do. Beds and a dining room come first.

plain.li: A bed for everyone and a table we all eat at. It's a home now.

warm.li: Look at it. Somebody walking past would think we'd always lived here.

cheerful.li: Real beds and a real table! I've been smiling all through supper.

cold.li: Everyone sleeps and eats properly now. I can start asking more of them.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a table for everyone
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Seat everyone together: a chair at an indoor table for everyone who eats, in a dining room with an impressiveness of at least 35.

plain.li: We eat in shifts, like a barracks. I'd like us all at one table, once a day.
Some of us eat standing up, plate in one hand. We need chairs, and enough of them.
[evening] Supper should be the best hour of the day. Right now it's a scramble for chairs.
[large] There are a lot of us now. We should still be able to sit down together.
[afterraid] After a day like today, I want everyone round one table where I can see them.

warm.li: At one table I'd see who's gone quiet and who isn't eating. Across three rooms, I can't.

blunt.li: I'm tired of eating off my knees. Build chairs.

cheerful.li: One long table with everyone at it, passing bowls and talking over each other!

gloomy.li: We hardly see each other except at work. Meals are all we have left.

cold.li: People who eat together argue less. I've watched it go both ways.

plain.li: Everyone at one table, and room to spare.

warm.li: I looked down the table tonight and every seat had someone I'm fond of in it.

cheerful.li: We were so loud at supper the animals came to look!

gloomy.li: Everyone fits. Give it a year and we'll be short of chairs again.

cold.li: A chair for everyone. I counted the chairs, then I counted us.

li.label: the first supper at the long table

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a calm season
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Fifteen days in a row without anyone having a mental break. A break starts the count again. Days off, good food, parties and fewer frictions all help. Proposed when someone is close to breaking, or the colony is worn down.

plain.li: Some of us are one bad day from snapping. I want fifteen days where nobody does.
Let's look after each other for a while. Rest, decent food, fewer arguments. See how long we can go.
[lowmood] I'm not doing well, and I'm not the only one. Let's slow down before someone breaks.
[afterraid] The raid shook everyone. Give us half a season of calm to get over it.
[winter] Winter wears on people. I'd like to reach the thaw with all of us in one piece.

warm.li: If you're struggling, say so, and one of us will sit with you until it passes.

blunt.li: Too many people are close to cracking. Fix that before it costs us.

cheerful.li: Let's all be nice to each other on purpose for fifteen days and see what happens!

gloomy.li: Somebody's going to break soon. I'd like to be wrong about that.

cold.li: When someone breaks, the rest of us spend days cleaning up after it. I'd rather spend them working.

plain.li: Fifteen days, and not one break. We're steadier than we were.

warm.li: I thanked each of you at breakfast this morning, and I meant it.

cheerful.li: Half a season without a single tantrum!

gloomy.li: Fifteen quiet days. I'll take them.

cold.li: Fifteen days without a break. Let's not undo it the first time the food runs short.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a year of steady nerves
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: A whole year (sixty days) without anyone in the colony having a mental break. A break starts the count again, so this is a long project for a colony that has learned to look after its people.

plain.li: We've lasted a year out here. I'd like the next one to go by without anyone breaking.
A whole year without anyone losing their head. It's never been done here. I'd like to try.
[highmood] Things are good right now. Let's keep them good, for a full year.
[spring] New year, new start. Let's see if we can get to next spring with steady nerves.

warm.li: We know each other well enough now to see someone struggling before they say a word.

blunt.li: Sixty days without anyone losing it. I'll do my part, and I expect you to do yours.

cheerful.li: A year of nobody throwing a fit! We'd deserve a feast at the end of it.

gloomy.li: A year is a long time out here. Something will go wrong. Maybe we can still hold together.

cold.li: Sixty days of uninterrupted work would be our best record by far.

plain.li: A full year without a single breakdown. We should write that down somewhere.

warm.li: A year of looking after each other. I couldn't ask for better people.

cheerful.li: A whole year! Somebody find a cake.

gloomy.li: A year without anyone breaking. I didn't think we'd make it.

cold.li: Sixty days without a break. I'll expect the same next year.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a healthy season
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Get the colony well and keep it that way: fifteen days in a row with nobody sick, and medicine on hand for the next time. Proposed while something is going round. Rest, warm beds, clean rooms and good food help.

plain.li: People are sniffling at every meal, and the rest of us will be soon.
Rest for the sick, warm beds, clean floors. Then fifteen days with nobody coughing.
[winter] Winter is when it spreads. We can't stop the cold, but we can stop passing things around.
[lowtech] Clean water, rest, and the sick kept apart. That's how the old healers did it.

warm.li: I hate seeing people cough their way through a shift. The sick should be in bed, with someone bringing them broth.

blunt.li: Sick people don't work. Get them well. Keep them well.

cheerful.li: I'll make soup for whoever's sick and keep it coming until they're up again.

gloomy.li: It's going round again. It always comes back if we don't deal with it.

cold.li: Sickness travels along the dinner table and through the barracks. Cut it off, and keep medicine back for the next one.

plain.li: Fifteen days without a cough or a fever. The infirmary is quiet for once.

warm.li: Everyone's well. I'd forgotten what that sounded like at breakfast.

cheerful.li: I haven't heard a sneeze in days. I keep listening for one.

cold.li: Everyone's fit for work again, and there's medicine set aside for the next time.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a proper infirmary
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: A real place for the sick and wounded, built in stages: medicine on hand first, then a room with two beds for patients, then that room kept clean enough that wounds don't fester.

plain.li: Right now our infirmary is wherever somebody falls down. I'd like a proper one.
Medicine first, then beds for the sick, then a room clean enough to cut someone open in.
[hurt] Look at this scar. That's what a dirty floor does to a clean cut.
[afterraid] We patched people up in the dining room again. That can't keep happening.
[small] With so few of us, one wound gone bad could empty a job nobody else knows how to do.

warm.li: I'd like whoever's hurt to have a door to close, and someone sitting with them.

blunt.li: People die of dirty wounds. Build an infirmary and keep it clean.

cheerful.li: I've been saving a bolt of clean cloth for exactly this. Bandages, sheets, the lot!

gloomy.li: We've lost people to wounds that should have healed. I don't want to lose any more that way.

cold.li: Most of the dead I've seen out here died of a wound gone bad, days after the fight.

plain.li: Medicine on the shelf, two clean beds, and a floor you could eat off. A proper infirmary.

warm.li: There's a stool by each bed now, for whoever sits up with the patient.

cheerful.li: I scrubbed it twice and it sparkles!

gloomy.li: It's ready, which means someone's about to need it.

cold.li: Two clean beds and the medicine to hand. Infections should drop.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: friends at the camp
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Strangers are camped on the map. Before they move on, three colonists should spend enough time at their fire to know them; the campers talk with whoever comes by.

plain.li: There are strangers camped out there and we've barely said a word to them. Let's go and sit at their fire.
They'll leave soon and carry stories of us wherever they go. Let's make them good stories.
[evening] Their fire is lit every evening. A few of us should go over and say hello.
[lowtech] Among my people, a stranger's fire is a place to trade news. We should trade some.

warm.li: They're far from home. A few friendly faces would mean a lot to them, and to us.

blunt.li: Go talk to the campers. Three of us, a few evenings. That's all.

cheerful.li: New people to talk to! I'm going tonight, who's coming?

gloomy.li: Better to have them as friends than as strangers watching us from the trees.

cold.li: Their people will hear how we treated them. I'd like what they hear to be useful to us.

plain.li: Three of us know the campers by name now. They waved when we passed.

warm.li: They're friends now, not strangers. I'll miss them when they go.

cheerful.li: They taught us a song and we taught them a worse one!

cold.li: They'll speak well of us to their people. I made sure of it.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: coats for winter
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Real cold is coming. Dress everyone warmly enough to stay comfortable at -10°C: parkas, cloaks, hats, whatever the colony can make.

plain.li: The first frost came early, and most of us are still dressed for summer.
Coats for everyone before the snow, or we'll be losing fingers by midwinter.
[fall] The birds are leaving and I can see my breath in the mornings. Coats, before the snow.
[tribal] Skins and furs, sewn double. That's how my people got through the long cold.
[medieval] Wool cloaks and hoods for every one of us. The tailor will be busy.

warm.li: I'd like to see us all come in from the fields with red cheeks and warm hands.

blunt.li: I'm not watching anyone else lose a finger because their sleeves were too short.

cheerful.li: Warm coats for everybody! We'll look like a herd of muffalo, but we'll be warm.

gloomy.li: Last winter took toes off somebody. I'd rather not count toes again.

cold.li: Frostbite cripples workers. Insulated clothing costs leather and a few days at the bench.

plain.li: Everyone's dressed for the cold, down to the last pair of mittens.

warm.li: Every one of us has a coat that fits. I checked the sleeves myself.

cheerful.li: We all look ridiculous and nobody's cold!

cold.li: Everyone has a coat. I've written down who got the good ones.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: the great feast
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: A feast for a big colony: a lavish meal for every colonist, and a dining room fine enough to eat it in.

plain.li: There are a lot of us now. I'd like to cook every one of us the best meal of their life, on the same night.
A lavish meal for everyone, in a hall that deserves it. We've earned a night like that.
[fall] The harvest is in. Let's have a feast worth remembering.
[rich] We can afford it. Let's spend some of it on ourselves.

warm.li: One night where everyone eats well and nobody works. I'd love to give the colony that.

blunt.li: A feast. Lavish meals for all of us. I'll cook.

cheerful.li: I've been writing menus in my head for weeks. Seven courses, and a pudding at the end!

gloomy.li: Who knows how many more chances we'll get. Let's have one good feast while we can.

cold.li: A feast costs us a week of ingredients and buys a month of people not complaining.

plain.li: A lavish meal for every one of us, and a hall to eat it in. The cooks have earned a day off.

warm.li: I watched them all eat and couldn't stop smiling. Worth every hour in the kitchen.

cheerful.li: I ate until I couldn't move, and then I had pudding!

cold.li: That feast will keep people agreeable for weeks. I'd call it cheap.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: nobody is the only one
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: In a small colony, losing the only doctor or the only cook can end it. Train a second person in each: two people at Medicine 6 or better, and two at Cooking 6 or better.

plain.li: If our doctor takes an arrow, who stitches the doctor? Nobody. That has to change.
There are so few of us that every job rests on one pair of hands. Let's double them up.
[hurt] I was the one who knew how to set a bone, and I was the one with the broken arm.
[afterraid] We nearly lost our cook in that raid. Who'd have fed us?

warm.li: I'd sleep better knowing any one of us could be looked after if the worst happened.

blunt.li: Two healers. Two cooks. No more jobs that only one of us can do.

cheerful.li: I'll teach anyone who'll sit still long enough, and I'll bring biscuits.

gloomy.li: We're one bad day away from nobody knowing how to do anything important.

cold.li: Lose our only cook and we'd be eating raw corn within the week. That's one arrow away.

plain.li: Two who can heal and two who can cook. We can lose a bad day now without losing everything.

warm.li: Our second cook made supper tonight without asking anyone a single question.

gloomy.li: Less fragile than we were.

cold.li: Any one of us could die now, and the rest would still eat and still be stitched up.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: word from outside
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: End the colony's isolation: build a comms console and make friends of two peoples abroad (goodwill 40 or more), so there's someone to call for trade or help.

plain.li: Nobody out there knows we exist, and we can't call anyone. That's how colonies vanish.
A comms console and a couple of friendly neighbors. Then if trouble comes, someone answers.
[afterraid] We could have used help yesterday, and there was no way to ask for it.
[small] As few as we are, we need friends more than walls.

warm.li: There are good people out there somewhere. I'd like to hear their voices.

blunt.li: We sit out here as if we were the last people alive. Build the console and talk to someone.

cheerful.li: Voices on the console every evening, and traders who know our name!

gloomy.li: We could shout all night out here and only the wind would hear us.

cold.li: A console costs a few components. Not having one could cost us the colony.

plain.li: Two neighbors who'll answer when we call. We're not alone out here.

warm.li: Friends abroad. It changes how the night sounds.

cheerful.li: I've talked to more strangers this week than in my whole life!

cold.li: Two factions will answer when we call. I've written down what each of them wants.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: ready for every season
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: A long project, in stages: food for thirty days put by, then everyone dressed for the cold, then medicine on the shelf, so the year can't catch the colony short.

plain.li: Every year we scramble for food in fall and coats at the first frost. Let's get ahead of it.
Food, warm clothes, medicine. One after another, and then the year can do its worst.
[spring] It's the start of the year. If we plan now, we won't be caught out by the end of it.
[poor] We can't afford to be caught short again. Let's put by what we need for the whole year.

warm.li: I'd like to sleep through a winter without worrying who'll go hungry or cold.

blunt.li: Stock up. All of it. Then stop panicking every season.

cheerful.li: A colony ready for anything! I'll make a list. Several lists.

gloomy.li: The year always finds the one thing we forgot. Let's forget less.

cold.li: Seasonal shortfalls are predictable. Prepare for them once and they stop being emergencies.

plain.li: Food put by, a coat on every back and medicine on the shelf.

warm.li: I walked through the storeroom and didn't find a single empty shelf.

cheerful.li: Every list ticked off, and I've started a new one for next year.

cold.li: Food, coats and medicine, all counted. The year can do as it likes.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: the healing garden
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Before industrial medicine, healing grows in the ground. Grow and dry twenty-five healroot, and train two people to Medicine 5 or better to use it.

plain.li: Healroot grows if you treat it right. A garden of it, and two of us who know how to use it.
Every colony that lasts has a healer and a garden. We have neither, yet.
[tribal] The healers of my people knew every root and leaf. I'd like us to learn half as much.
[spring] Planting season. If we put healroot in now, we'll have medicine by fall.

warm.li: I want to be able to help when someone's hurt, not just hold their hand.

blunt.li: Grow healroot. Learn to use it. Stop dying of small things.

cheerful.li: Healroot smells like wet socks, and I want a whole garden of it!

gloomy.li: Without medicine, a scratch can kill you out here. I've seen it happen.

cold.li: Herbal medicine and trained hands halve the deaths from infection.

plain.li: Healroot hanging in bundles and two of us who know what to do with it.

warm.li: The next time someone's hurt, I'll know which root to reach for.

gloomy.li: Something will still get us. Not a scratch, though.

cold.li: Twenty-five healroot, dried, and two people who won't waste it.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: whole again
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Give back what the colony's people have lost: a replacement for every missing limb or eye the colony can make or has in stock. Proposed when someone is missing a part that can be replaced.

plain.li: Some of us are missing an arm or an eye, and we have what it takes to give them back.
Nobody here should have to limp when we can make them a leg.
[hurt] I know what it's like to lose part of yourself. Let's give back what we can.
[spacer] We have the means to make people whole. Leaving them broken is a choice.

warm.li: They gave a piece of themselves for this colony. The least we can do is give it back.

blunt.li: We have the parts and we have the hands. Stop making them limp.

cheerful.li: I want to see everyone running again. Races at the next party!

gloomy.li: Every fight takes something from someone. At least this part we can fix.

cold.li: A one-handed colonist does half the work and eats the whole meal.

plain.li: All of them have what they lost back, near enough.

warm.li: Watching them walk without a crutch was worth all the work.

cheerful.li: Someone challenged me to a race this morning, on their new leg!

cold.li: All replaceable losses replaced.
